title.narrative: Integrated Nutrition response to drought affected communities in Baidoa rural Bay region

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtThe project aims to provide integrated emergency response on nutrition services through establishment of eight mobile nutrition and one static nutrition center in Baidoa rural Bay region Somalia. The project overall beneficiary is 11,600 that is (4,000 Boys, 4,000 Girls and 3,600 PLW), the nutrition intervention intends to achieve comprehensive community outreach outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) integrated supplementary feeding program. HIDIG endeavor to provide adequate caregivers infant and young child feeding practices, IYCF/NHHP promotion session for better information dissemination to the caregivers in the project area, Referral of malnourished children with severely complicated cases will be done to the target under five boys and girls as well as providing multiple micronutrient , iron folic , deworming and vitamin A supplementation to both lt5children boys, girls and PLW including 15% disable group, HIDIG will ensure to engage community nutrition volunteers lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtthrough provision of monthly mass screening and referral services, However, it will also ensure to undertake Nutrition activities that will be integrated in the sense that under five children boys, girls admitted at the OTP sites will be immunized against measles and other communicable disease and as well the SAM complicated cases referred to the Bay referral hospital in Baidoa town for proper medical treatment, on the same note pregnant mothers requiring ANC/PNC will be provided both NHHP/IYCF-E and be integrated with hygiene promotions activities such as hand washing practices and shall be linked with HIDIG health projects in Baidoa rural to ensure area based services coordination. HIDIG will ensure protection services mainstreaming into its nutrition services points as well as training its project staff with the necessary protection services linkages to enhanced child protection, HDIG will also trained its nutrition volunteers and staff on Mother led MUAC screening to enable accelerate referral pathways between the organization services points to the various rural location hence strengthening quick identification of severely and moderately malnourished children while improving the referral system for the treatment and prevention of malnutrition. lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gt
